provider.name: Avibase
provider.organization_type: global bird taxonomy, nomenclature, checklist, and multilingual names database
provider.description: Avibase is a global bird database that reconciles taxonomic concepts and nomenclature across major authorities, provides regional checklists, multilingual common names, species records, and persistent identifiers for avian taxa.
institutional_context: Historical Bird Studies Canada / Études d'Oiseaux Canada branding may appear in older pages

purpose.summary: This file is a crawl-ready source catalog for collecting Avibase documentation, taxonomy and checklist guidance, multilingual-name documentation, authority mappings, downloads, APIs, legal terms, citation instructions, and institutional context.
purpose.authoritative_notice: Avibase and its supporting institution remain authoritative for taxonomic concepts, checklists, names, identifiers, citation, rights, terms, and contact information.

review.notes: Primary Avibase website and documentation discovery root.
Project purpose, history, scope, taxonomy sources, editorial background, and institutional context.
Official contact information, corrections, technical support, and institutional correspondence.
Global bird taxonomy, accepted taxa, synonyms, alternate treatments, and classification.
Discovery seed for taxonomic concept identifiers, synonymy, splits, lumps, and checklist reconciliation.
Country, region, and subnational bird checklists.
World checklist entry point; query parameters and current defaults require live verification.
Search interface for scientific names, common names, synonyms, and Avibase identifiers.
Discovery seed for species records, names, taxonomy, distribution, and checklist associations.
Discovery seed for multilingual common names, language codes, translations, and vernacular-name conventions.
Geographic units, countries, territories, states, provinces, and regional hierarchy.
Discovery seed for IOC, Clements/eBird, BirdLife/HBW, Howard and Moore, regional authorities, and comparison methodology.
Discovery seed for downloadable checklists, exports, data files, and bulk-access conditions.
Discovery seed for documented APIs, web services, query parameters, data feeds, and machine-readable outputs.
User guide, search help, checklist instructions, field definitions, and troubleshooting.
Frequently asked questions, project explanation, taxonomy, names, and data-use guidance.
Preferred citation, access-date guidance, authorship, versioning, and attribution.
Discovery seed for terms, disclaimers, acceptable use, and database access restrictions.
Copyright, database rights, checklist reuse, redistribution, and permission requirements.
Discovery seed for privacy, cookies, analytics, and personal-data processing.
Announcements, taxonomy updates, checklist releases, and project changes.
Parent or supporting institutional context, organizational information, and contact details.
Parent-institution privacy policy; verify applicability to Avibase.
Crawler access rules; evaluate before recursive acquisition.
Optional machine-readable discovery source; may not exist or may redirect.

notes: Do not infer that JSP query interfaces constitute a supported public API.
Record only explicitly documented programmatic interfaces or stable downloadable products.
Capture parameters, identifiers, response schemas, versioning, authentication, limits, and legal conditions.
Capture exact official legal wording before normalizing rights metadata.
Separate Avibase identifiers and reconciliation work from third-party taxonomic authority content.
Regional checklists, names, and downloadable files may have different reuse conditions.
Do not assume parent-institution terms fully describe Avibase-specific data rights.
Seed URLs are best-effort and were not live-verified in this session.
The acquisition program should update retrieval, content, review, and verification fields in place.
Some JSP paths or query forms may redirect, be renamed, or require parameters; preserve redirect and failure metadata.
Do not recursively crawl every species, checklist, region, or language page when the task is documentation acquisition.
Do not store API keys, passwords, cookies, OAuth tokens, or session credentials in this JSON file.
Avibase reconciliation content, third-party authority treatments, names, regional checklists, and downloads may carry different rights.
